decisions.reason: As a low-cost automation extension in a slow-moving municipal infrastructure market, it still has option value and has shown no clear failure signal.
The planner-focused web tool is inexpensive to maintain and can support project acquisition, so it is worth keeping while demand continues to emerge.
Although a physical product is costlier to support than software, this flap weir is close to the core portfolio and one year is too early to judge it in long public procurement cycles.
The energy management system is strongly aligned with the firm's strategic direction toward digitally networked and efficient water infrastructure, so keeping the option open is attractive.
The overflow flap gate line has clear fit with core water-level-control applications and the dedicated multi-model rollout suggests enough commitment to keep it on the market.
